# Velocity against time

<!-- STEP id="steady" -->
A car moves at a steady 72 km/h, that is, 20 m/s. Its velocity-time graph is a flat line. The velocity is constant, so the acceleration is zero.

<!-- STEP id="rising" -->
A second car starts from rest and gains 2.5 m/s every 5 s (Table 4.5). Its graph is a rising straight line: a constant acceleration in the direction of the velocity.

<!-- STEP id="falling" -->
A third car starts at 15 m/s and loses 2.5 m/s every 5 s (Table 4.6). Its graph is a falling straight line: a constant acceleration opposite to the velocity.
